styleGuide: Use the supplied note examples as writing and layout references only; never copy their applicants, bank details, amounts, dates, approval marks or head-of-account codes.
Begin with an office-routing heading and an underlined subject, followed by a compact particulars table where useful.
Write concise third-person administrative prose covering receipt, the applicant's circumstances and the factual / financial examination.
Distinguish the applicant's statements from verified University records. Do not claim a receipt, enclosure or verification exists merely because it is customary.

Do not append missing-information lists, generic conditional recommendations, standard closings, disclaimers or caveat footers. Keep the note focused on its substantive facts and analysis. Do not grant sanction, sign, post payments, invent policy numbers, or carry example facts into a new proposal.

profiles.title: Fee refund noting
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Internal Audit / Cashier / Concerned Section
profiles.examination: Verify the payment against receipts and the institutional ledger, reconcile the amount claimed, check for a prior refund or reversal, and identify the applicable refund policy and authorised accounting head before release.

profiles.title: Admission withdrawal / refund noting
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Academic Section / Internal Audit
profiles.examination: The financial examination covers the admission and withdrawal dates, payment received, session-specific refund provisions, permissible deductions and any earlier refund.

profiles.title: Hostel refund noting
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Student Welfare / Hostel Warden / Internal Audit
profiles.examination: Obtain the hostel allotment and vacation / clearance particulars, confirm payment and outstanding dues, and examine refund eligibility under the applicable hostel rules before recommending an amount.

profiles.title: Unprovided service / analysis-fee refund noting
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Concerned Department / Internal Audit
profiles.examination: Verify the requisition, payment and department's confirmation of the service not being provided; check any work already performed, prior refunds and the applicable service-refund provisions.

profiles.title: GPF examination in the supplied administrative-note format
profiles.routing: Registrar / Finance & Accounts / Internal Audit / Concerned Section
profiles.examination: The GPF examination concerns the type of request, subscriber particulars, purpose, fund balance and recovery terms.

profiles.title: Consultancy examination in the supplied administrative-note format
profiles.routing: Head / Director / Registrar / Advisory Committee, Consultancy Services / Finance & Accounts
profiles.examination: Examine the proposed consultancy assignment, client, scope, period, facilities and financial terms. Confirm the appropriate category and obtain the prescribed recommendations, approvals and supporting records before acceptance or release of earnings.

profiles.title: Procurement examination in the supplied administrative-note format
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Purchase Section / Concerned Department / Competent Authority
profiles.examination: The procurement examination covers the stated need, specifications and quantity, estimated expenditure, budget availability, and the proposed sourcing method. Examine the supplied quotations or bid records, price comparison, delivery and acceptance terms, and the applicable procurement provisions and delegation of financial authority.

profiles.title: General administrative examination
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Concerned Section / Competent Authority
profiles.examination: The proposal is placed for examination of the requested action and its factual and financial basis.

rules.title: Rule 5 · Subscriber eligibility
rules.excerpt: Every employee of the University holding a permanent substantive appointment and a subscriber to C.P.F before 1-2-2005 and not retired from the service of the university till 31.03.2013 shall be entitled to be a subscriber to the General Provident Fund.

rules.title: Rule 12.1 · Advance sanctioning authority
rules.excerpt: The payment of an advance from the fund may be sanctioned by the Vice-Chancellor to a subscriber from the amount of his subscription and interest thereon standing to his credit, subject to the following conditions.

rules.title: Rule 12.1.1 · Permitted advance purposes
rules.excerpt:
No advance shall be granted unless the sanctioning authority is satisfied that the applicant's pecuniary circumstance justifies it, and that it will be spent for the following purpose and not otherwise:
(i) To pay expenses incurred in connection with the illness of the subscriber, subscriber's wife, legitimate children, stepmother, parents, sisters and minor brother actually dependent on him.
(ii) To pay obligatory expenses in connection with subscriber's marriage, funerals or ceremonies which by his religion it is incumbent on him to perform.
(iii) To meet the cost of higher education of any person actually dependent on the subscriber.
(iv) To meet the cost of legal proceeding instituted by the applicant for vindicating his position in regard to any allegations made against him in respect of any act done or purporting to be done by him in the discharge of his official duty. The advance is not admissible for proceedings unconnected with official duty or against the University concerning conditions of service or penalty.
(v) To meet the cost of his defence where the applicant is prosecuted by the University in respect of any alleged official misconduct on his part.

rules.title: Rules 12.1.2–12.1.3 · Advance ceiling and previous advance
rules.excerpt:
12.1.2 An advance shall in no case exceed 50 percent of the amount of subscription and interest thereon standing to the credit of the subscriber in the Fund.
12.1.3 An advance shall not be granted to any subscriber in excess of the limit laid down in Rule 12.1.2 herein or until repayment of the previous advance.

rules.title: Rule 12.1.4 · Principal instalments
rules.excerpt: The amount of advance shall be recovered in not more than thirty six equal monthly installments. Each installment shall be a number of whole rupees, the amount of advance being raised or reduced, if necessary, to admit of the fixation of such installments. A subscriber may at his option repay in a smaller number of installments or in a lump sum.

rules.title: Rule 12.1.5 · Commencement of recovery
rules.excerpt: Recovery of advance shall be made from the monthly pay of a subscriber and shall commence on the first occasion, after the advance is made, on which the subscriber draws pay for a full month.

rules.title: Rule 12.1.6 · Interest on advances
rules.excerpt: Interest on advances shall be such as may be determined by the University from time to time and shall not exceed by more than two percent of the rate paid by the University to the account of a subscriber. The interest shall ordinarily be recovered in one installment from pay in the next month after complete repayment of the principal has been made. If the period of repayments exceeds twenty months, interest may, if the subscriber so desires, be recovered in two equal monthly installments, rounded to the nearest whole rupee.

rules.title: Rules 13.1–13.1.1 · Withdrawal eligibility and authority
rules.excerpt:
13.1 Subject to the conditions specified below withdrawal from the Fund may be sanctioned by the Vice-Chancellor at any time.
13.1.1 After the completion of twenty five years of service (including broken period of service, if any) of a subscriber or within three years before the date of his retirement on superannuation, whichever is earlier, from the amount standing to his credit in the Fund, for one or more of the specified purposes.

rules.title: Rule 13.1.1(a)–(f) · Withdrawal purposes
rules.excerpt: Permitted withdrawal purposes in Rule 13.1.1 include higher education of an actually dependent child (courses outside India beyond High School, or medical, engineering or other technical or specialised courses in India beyond High School lasting at least three years); marriage of a son or daughter, or if there is no daughter another dependent female relation; illness of the subscriber or an actually dependent person including necessary travel; acquiring, constructing or modifying a residence, purchasing its site, or repaying specified housing loans. See pages 8–9 of the supplied rulebook for the complete wording and conditions.

rules.title: Rule 13.2 · Withdrawal limit
rules.excerpt: Any sum withdrawn by a subscriber at any one time for one or more of the purposes specified in Rule 13.1.1 from the amount standing to his credit in the Fund shall not exceed three fourth of such amount or twenty month's pay of the subscriber, whichever is less.

rules.title: Rule 14.1 · Final payment on leaving service
rules.excerpt: When a subscriber quits the service of the University, the amount standing to his credit in the Fund shall become payable to him. Rule 14.1.1 contains conditions for repayment if a dismissed subscriber is reinstated.

rules.title: Rule 15.1 · Retirement while on leave or medical unfitness
rules.excerpt: When a subscriber while on leave has been permitted to retire or has been declared by the prescribed competent medical authority to be unfit for further service, the amount standing to his credit in the Fund shall, upon an application to the Registrar, become payable to the subscriber.

rules.title: Rule 2.1 · Administration and prior approval
rules.excerpt: Summary of pages 2–3: Consultancy is administered by the Advisory Committee chaired by the Dean, Research and Development. DMC/BoM manages departmental day-to-day administrative and financial matters; the Registrar or a delegated officer does so for non-teaching officers. All assignments require prior University approval after Advisory Committee recommendation and must not detract from primary duties. Assignments remain University consultancy irrespective of the extent of University facilities used.
rules.application: Under Rules 2.1 and 2.2, confirm the concerned DMC/BoM or Registrar routing, Advisory Committee recommendation and prior University approval, with no detriment to primary duties.

rules.title: Rule 2.2 · Acceptance and recommendations
rules.excerpt: Summary: Assignments require University approval on recommendation of the concerned DMC/BoM and the Chairperson, Advisory Committee, Consultancy Services. They should generally be reported in advance to the Chairperson and concerned Head/Director. Where client and consultant are close relatives, the Chairperson must vet the assignment before acceptance.
rules.application: Check the prescribed recommendations and advance reporting under Rule 2.2; any close-relative relationship requires Chairperson vetting before acceptance.

rules.title: Rule 2.1.1 · Consultancy Fund and billing
rules.excerpt: The Consultancy Charges/Fees shall be deposited in the Dibrugarh University Consultancy Fund (DUCF). Bills/claims are to be made in quadruplicate for the client, Secretary of the Advisory Committee, concerned School/Department/Centre for Studies, and faculty member(s) assigned the consultancy work.
rules.application: Verify deposit of consultancy charges in DUCF and the four billing/record copies required by Rule 2.1.1.

rules.title: Rule 2.1.2 · Distribution of earnings
rules.excerpt: The earnings distribution table allocates 60% to consultants and laboratory staff including additional/non-teaching staff (if any), and 40% to the University. Within the 60% group share, 60% is for consultants and 40% for laboratory/additional/non-teaching staff (if any). Distribution is subject to submission of the report to the client/organization under intimation to the Advisory Committee.
rules.application: Rule 2.1.2 allocates 60% to the consultants/staff group and 40% to the University. The group share is divided 60:40 between consultants and eligible staff. Distribution follows submission of the client report with intimation to the Advisory Committee.

rules.title: Rule 2.1.2 · Patent profits and University-share uses
rules.excerpt: Summary: The University's share may support new/interdisciplinary research facilities, library grants, patent filing, visiting industry experts and faculty consultancy-related industry visits. Where consultancy results in a patent, profits from the innovation are shared equally among the individual/group of faculty, University and client.
rules.application: Distinguish ordinary consultancy earnings from patent-derived profits under Rule 2.1.2; examine the specified uses of the University's share and the equal three-party patent-profit provision where relevant.

rules.title: Rule 2.3 · Off-campus TA/DA
rules.excerpt: For consultancy outside the University campus, consultants and accompanying staff are entitled to normal University TA/DA subject to availability of money in DUCF and endorsement of the Advisory Committee, Consultancy Services.
rules.application: For off-campus travel, Rule 2.3 requires normal University TA/DA rates, available DUCF funds and Advisory Committee endorsement; obtain the current rates rather than inventing an allowance.

rules.title: Rule 2.4 · Client hospitality
rules.excerpt: Prospective clients may receive local hospitality in the University's Guest House, but all such expenses are to be borne by the client at DU official rates.
rules.application: Under Rule 2.4, confirm that client hospitality costs are borne by the client at the University's official rates.

rules.title: Rules 2.5.1–2.5.3 · Tax provisions
rules.excerpt: In the supplied edition, Rules 2.5.1–2.5.3 address income-tax deduction at source, service tax and other applicable taxes. Rule 2.5.2 states a service-tax figure of 12.24% of consultancy fees, payable by the client in addition to consultancy charges.
rules.application: Rules 2.5.1–2.5.3 address tax deductions and the service-tax provisions in the supplied edition.

rules.title: Rules 1 and 2.6 · Fixation of consultancy fees
rules.excerpt: Summary of pages 1 and 5: Consultancy charges are determined by the Advisory Committee in consultation with consultants and the client. Fee components may include visits, materials, temporary staff, fieldwork, additional equipment/infrastructure, progress-report preparation and other assignment-related expenses.
rules.application: Under Rules 1 and 2.6, confirm Advisory Committee determination of fees with the consultant and client, supported by the relevant cost components.

rules.title: Rule 2.7 · Special Consultancy Leave
rules.excerpt: Summary of pages 5–6: Consultants and staff may ordinarily spend at most 20 days per calendar year on consultancy visits outside the University, treated as Special Consultancy Leave in addition to ordinary leave entitlements. It cannot be availed for more than 5 days at a time. University sanction requires the recommendation of the Chairperson, Advisory Committee, Consultancy Services.
rules.application: Check Rule 2.7 against the consultancy-leave record: ordinarily at most 20 days in a calendar year and no more than 5 days at a time, with Chairperson recommendation and University sanction.

rules.title: Rule 3(i) · Individual / personal / retainer consultancy
rules.excerpt: Summary: This category does not use University facilities or human resources. Prior University permission on Chairperson recommendation is required in the prescribed proforma through the DMC/BoM or Registrar, indicating work, period and fees. Reports must be filed and sent to the Chairperson, with provisions for classified reports. Total yearly fees for individual/retainer consultancy must not exceed the consultant's gross annual University salary.
rules.application: For an individual/retainer assignment under Rule 3(i), confirm the resource-use classification, prescribed permission and report records, and compare total yearly consultancy fees with gross annual University salary.

rules.title: Rule 3(ii) · Institutional consultancy
rules.excerpt: Summary of pages 6–7: Institutional consultancy uses University facilities including human resources. The Chairperson identifies the department/centre/consultants after consulting the client. The Head/Director or Registrar assigns work after DMC/BoM consultation. Prescribed permission must enclose the client's authorizing letter; relevant records are retained and copies sent to the Chairperson.
rules.application: Where University facilities or staff are to be used, examine institutional consultancy under Rule 3(ii), including client authorization, identification/assignment of work and prescribed permission.

rules.title: Rule 3(iii) · Routine consultancy and standard rates
rules.excerpt: Summary: Routine consultancy may include testing, calibration, fabrication, project evaluation, material analysis, feasibility reports, study materials, external students' training/dissertation/report preparation, and technical advice, without in-depth studies or further processing of test results. The Head/Director draws up standard rates in consultation with the Chairperson. The rules for category (i) also govern this category.
rules.application: For routine consultancy, Rule 3(iii) requires standard rates drawn up by the Head/Director in consultation with the Chairperson and also applies the rules of category (i); confirm the actual nature and extent of the work.

rules.title: Rule 4 · Reports and maintenance of records
rules.excerpt: Departments/centres/consultants submit half-yearly reports to the Chairperson with a copy to the Vice-Chancellor. Reports to clients are filed with the department/centre and sent to the Chairperson. Annual consultancy earnings and DUCF utilization are reported half-yearly to the Executive Council.
rules.application: Ensure the client-report copies and half-yearly reporting/DUCF records required by Rule 4 are maintained.

rules.title: Assam Rule 3 · Need, specifications and realistic estimate
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Procurement must be essential for public service. State the quality, quantity and scope without superfluous features or idle inventory; consider sustainability, maintenance and compatibility. Specifications should support competition and value for money, and the estimated cost must be realistic and objectively assessed. Preserve the need-assessment records.
rules.application: Assam Rule 3 requires the proposal's public need, quantity, specifications, compatibility and realistic cost estimate to be examined together; avoid unnecessary features, excess quantities and idle inventory.

rules.title: Assam Rule 4 · Procurement plan and funding
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: The procurement plan records goods/works/services, purpose, essentiality, specifications, estimated value, source of funds, procurement method and reasons for an alternative to open competitive bidding, bidder limitations and time frames. Approved plans and updates are uploaded within seven days, subject to the stated provisions. Bodies must also obtain their applicable governing-body approvals.
rules.application: Under Assam Rule 4, relate the requirement to the approved procurement plan, funding source, proposed method and delivery or completion schedule, recording reasons for an alternative to open competitive bidding.

rules.title: Assam Rule 8 · Approvals, sanctions and delegated powers
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Obtain required approvals and sanctions under the applicable financial rules and delegated powers, with available funds. Works ordinarily require administrative approval and technical sanction before inviting bids. Goods/services require financial sanction before bid acceptance or supply order. The rule separately specifies limited advance preparatory action and its approvals. Do not divide or bulk procurement after bids have been invited.
rules.application: Assam Rule 8 requires available funds and the appropriate delegated financial authority. Distinguish works administrative approval/technical sanction from goods or services financial sanction, and verify the required approvals before bid acceptance or issue of an order.

rules.title: Assam Rule 13 · Clear specifications and equivalent products
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Describe the subject matter clearly and without ambiguity, including relevant technical, qualitative and performance characteristics. Avoid restrictive brand names or catalogue references except in the specified single-source situations; where unavoidable, use the words 'or substantially equivalent'.
rules.application: Under Assam Rule 13, examine whether the specification is clear and performance-based, and whether any brand restriction has an applicable justification or the required substantially-equivalent provision.

rules.title: Assam Rule 24 · Procurement method and recorded reasons
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Follow the procedure for the chosen procurement method. Open competitive bidding is the preferred method; specific reasons and circumstances for an alternative must be recorded in the case file and procurement register with the deciding authority's name and designation.
rules.application: Assam Rule 24 makes open competitive bidding the preferred method. Examine the proposed method and record the specific reasons, circumstances and competent decision supporting any alternative.

rules.title: Assam Rules 5, 6 and 12 · Bidder eligibility and integrity
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Examine bidder eligibility/debarment and applicable joint-venture conditions. Disclose and address conflicts of interest, including common control and participation in preparing specifications. Procuring personnel and bidders must follow the code of integrity, equal treatment, confidentiality and the declared evaluation criteria.
rules.application: Examine the proposed bidders' eligibility and conflicts under Assam Rules 5 and 6, and the equal-treatment, confidentiality and integrity requirements under Rule 12.

rules.title: Assam Rules 9 and 11 · Procurement records and registers
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Maintain procurement, vendor, purchase-order, progress, stock, asset and liability records as applicable, with authentication, verification and audit availability. Preserve the procurement proceedings, bidder prices, evaluation record, successful-bid details and reasons for cancellation under the prescribed record-retention rules.
rules.application: Assam Rules 9 and 11 require the procurement proceedings and applicable order, stock, asset, payment and liability records to remain traceable and available for verification and audit.

rules.title: Assam Rules 14–15 · Bid envelopes and evaluation criteria
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Choose the prescribed single/two-envelope procedure according to the requirement's technical complexity. Evaluate technical bids before accessing financial bids in a two-envelope process. Apply only the declared, verifiable evaluation criteria; for non-consultancy procurement, compare prices among eligible and technically/commercially compliant bids.
rules.application: Under Assam Rules 14 and 15, establish the appropriate bid-envelope process and evaluate only against the disclosed eligibility and technical/commercial criteria before comparing qualifying prices.

rules.title: Assam Rule 16 · Restricted price negotiations
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Except for the specified single-source/competitive-negotiation provisions, negotiations are restricted. Competent-authority-approved negotiation with the lowest or most advantageous responsive bidder is permitted in the stated circumstances such as suspected cartel prices or unreasonable rates; record the reasons and results. The rule specifies notice periods and written revised bids.
rules.application: Assam Rule 16 requires the permitted grounds, prior competent approval and written record for any proposed price negotiation; the lowest quotation alone does not authorize unrestricted negotiations.

rules.title: Assam Rule 17 · State procurement portal and exceptions
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary of PDF pages 17–19 (scanned out of printed-page order): Publish prescribed procurement information and decisions on the State Public Procurement Portal, with the stated confidentiality and authentication provisions. Rule 17(8) lists exceptions for RFQ, spot purchase, GeM, community procurement, e-commerce and construction-committee procurements; examine the specific method's rules.
rules.application: Check Assam Rule 17's publication requirements against the actual procurement method, including its express exceptions; apply the method-specific requirements rather than assuming every route has identical portal obligations.

rules.title: Assam Rule 24(A) · Open competitive bidding
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Eligible bidders may participate without restriction in open competitive bidding. The supplied edition specifies at least 21 clear days from the latest advertisement to opening for open competitive bidding and at least 45 clear days for international competitive bidding, whose stated grounds must be met.
rules.application: For open competitive bidding, examine participation and the clear-day timetable under Assam Rule 24(A), including the separate grounds and timetable for an international invitation.

rules.title: Assam Rule 24(B) · Limited bidding
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Limited bidding requires satisfaction of the Act's stated conditions and recorded reasons. Specify the bidder limitation criteria and select bidders fairly. The open-competitive procedure generally applies with the stated modifications, including participation of bidders meeting the qualification/limitation criteria even if not individually invited.
rules.application: Under Assam Rule 24(B), establish the permissible grounds for limited bidding and the declared limitation criteria; document fair selection and participation of qualifying bidders.

rules.title: Assam Rule 24(C) · Single source and proprietary articles
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Single-source procurement requires the Act's permitted circumstances and recorded grounds for selecting the bidder. OEM/proprietary-right purchases require a Proprietary Article Certificate signed under the appropriate schedule of powers. Apply the stated publication exceptions, reasonableness/negotiation provisions and reporting requirements.
rules.application: Assam Rule 24(C) requires a recorded single-source justification and, where relevant, a properly authorized Proprietary Article Certificate; identify the approving power and examine price reasonableness.

rules.title: Assam Rule 24(D) · Two-stage bidding
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: For complex requirements, the first stage seeks technical solutions and qualifications without bid prices. Shortlist against disclosed criteria, provide equal opportunity in discussions, and invite final priced bids against the revised specifications in the second stage, subject to the rule's alternatives and withdrawal conditions.
rules.application: Where two-stage bidding is proposed, Assam Rule 24(D) requires a technical first stage without price and a properly documented transition to the final priced stage.

rules.title: Assam Rule 24(F) · Request for quotations
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: In the supplied 2020 edition, RFQ requires estimated cost/value less than INR 100000 on one occasion and no more than INR 500000 in a financial year, subject to Finance Department changes. Seek sealed quotations from at least three genuine potential bidders, retain market-enquiry records, compare responsive prices and prepare a committee-signed comparative statement. Do not split demand to avoid higher approval or competitive bidding.
rules.application: Where RFQ is proposed, Assam Rule 24(F) specifies less than INR 100000 per occasion and an INR 500000 financial-year ceiling in the supplied edition. Examine the annual procurement record, at least three requested sealed quotations, market-price reasonableness and the signed comparative statement.

rules.title: Assam Rule 24(G) · Spot purchase
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Spot purchase uses the RFQ value limits as duly notified. The Spot Purchase Committee surveys specifications, quality and prevailing dealer/wholesale rates, recommends a reliable supplier, records its jointly signed certificate and retains the dealer/price enquiry records.
rules.application: For spot purchase, examine the applicable notified limit and the committee's market survey, supplier recommendation and signed certificate under Assam Rule 24(G).

rules.title: Assam Rule 24(I)(1) · Rate contracts
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Rate contracts are ordinarily established by open competitive bidding without a committed procurement quantity. Subsequent orders use the contracted rates/terms as needs arise. State approximate requirements, specifications and contract period in the bid documents; the supplied rule normally uses one financial year and states conditions for shorter periods or extension.
rules.application: For a rate-contract purchase, examine both the competitively established contract and the proposed call-off's quantity, validity, rates, delivery location and schedule under Assam Rule 24(I)(1).

rules.title: Assam Rule 24(I)(2) · Government e-Marketplace
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: GeM may be used for available essential common-use requirements subject to the Act and State guidelines. The offered rate/total cost must not exceed prevailing State wholesale or authorized-dealer discounted rates. Publish annual requirements within 30 days of budget approval, avoid piecemeal splitting and obtain prior sanction under delegated powers. Finance may notify detailed procedures and ceilings.
rules.application: For GeM procurement, Assam Rule 24(I)(2) requires prior sanction, comparison with relevant market/dealer rates and aggregation of demand; use the applicable State-notified procedures and ceilings.

rules.title: Assam Rule 25 · Hiring consultancy and non-consultancy services
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Public-interest hiring must define the essential service, outputs and completion period. Consultancy engagement requires the prescribed prior approval and objective/scope/cost/qualification assessment; EOI, shortlisting and TOR procedures follow Rule 25. Non-consultancy services have physical/measurable deliverables and are distinguished from advisory/intellectual consultancy.
rules.application: For external service engagement, apply Assam Rule 25 to the defined outputs, period, cost estimate, qualifications, prior approval and appropriate selection/TOR process; this is procurement of a service rather than distribution of University consultancy earnings.

rules.title: Assam Rule 29 · Bid security
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: The supplied edition generally sets bid security at 2–5% of estimated procurement value, with the exact amount rounded to the nearest thousand rupees and stated in the bid documents, subject to notified concessions/limits. Security ordinarily remains valid 28 days beyond bid validity. Verify guarantees and apply the stated release/forfeiture provisions.
rules.application: Examine Assam Rule 29's bid-security basis, specified amount, instrument, concessions and 28-day additional validity; do not substitute the central works manual's different validity period.

rules.title: Assam Rule 30 · Performance security
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Obtain performance security before award/signing. The supplied edition requires at least 5% of the supply/work-order value, or higher where the bid documents specify, in an accepted form. Validity extends at least 60 days beyond all contractual obligations, including warranty, maintenance and defect liability, whichever is latest; amendments may be notified.
rules.application: Assam Rule 30 requires the applicable performance-security amount and instrument before award, with validity beyond the latest contractual, warranty or defect-liability obligation.

rules.title: Assam Rule 31 · Agreement and order
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Following acceptance by the competent authority, issue written intimation with the sanction/approval terms and require agreement and performance security within the bid-document period, or 15 days from dispatch of acceptance when unspecified. The procurement contract comes into force from issue of the work/supply order. Apply the prescribed action for failure to sign or furnish security.
rules.application: Under Assam Rule 31, distinguish a draft recommendation from competent acceptance, the signed agreement/security requirements and the subsequent work or supply order.

rules.title: Assam Rule 33 · Repeat orders
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Repeat orders for goods/services require an original open-competitive order and provision in the bid documents, the same rates/terms, a recorded assessment that fresh procurement would not yield better prices, and compliance with the Finance-notified percentage limit. Place them within six months of expiry of the original contract.
rules.application: For repeat orders, verify Assam Rule 33's original bidding provision, unchanged rates/terms, recorded price assessment, notified percentage limit and time window.

rules.title: Works Manual 1.3 · Scope and type of works
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Works include civil/mechanical/electrical construction, repair, renovation and related operations; distinguish original, minor and repair works. The manual addresses Central Government entities and substantially centrally owned/controlled/assisted bodies, subject to their applicable departmental rules and approved autonomous-body provisions. Internationally financed projects may follow agreed procurement procedures.
rules.application: Works Manual 1.3 requires the work's nature and the applicable institutional/departmental framework to be established before applying the central works procedures.

rules.title: Works Manual 1.10 · Prerequisites before commencing work
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Assess existing assets, need and resources; do not split a project to bypass higher sanction. Ordinarily obtain the DPR, administrative approval, expenditure sanction, technical approval, funds, duly processed tender, contract/work order, land and statutory clearances before commencing work or incurring liability. The manual separately states the urgency exception and simultaneous approval/accounting actions.
rules.application: Under Works Manual 1.10, examine the integrated project and the status of DPR, administrative/expenditure/technical approvals, funds, land and clearances before commencement; avoid splitting the work to bypass sanction.

rules.title: Works Manual 2.2–2.4 · Preliminary and detailed project reports
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: The PPR/rough estimate records need, scope, exclusions, land, services, concept plans, cost basis, cash flow and funding. Seek in-principle approval before the DPR, which covers engineering scope, estimates, completion period, land/statutory matters, allocation, monitoring and quality systems. Paragraph 2.4 describes a PPR-based exception for repair works up to INR 3000000 in the supplied edition.
rules.application: Use Works Manual 2.2–2.4 to examine the proposal's scope, estimate basis, drawings, land/services, funding and completion schedule, distinguishing preliminary acceptance of need from the detailed project approval.

rules.title: Works Manual 2.5–2.7 · Sanctions, designs and funds
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Administrative approval/expenditure sanction follows examination of DPR/estimates; the sanction records scope, estimated cost, completion time and funding shares. Obtain coordinated detailed designs/estimates and technical sanction, with the EPC exception and executing-agency responsibilities described in the manual. Ensure funds and realistic year-wise requirements before execution.
rules.application: Works Manual 2.5–2.7 requires separate examination of administrative approval, expenditure sanction, technical design/estimate approval and available funds, with the proposed scope, cost and completion period stated.

rules.title: Works Manual 3.5.1 · Open tendering
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Open tender enquiry is the default competitive route; the supplied 2019 edition describes OTE for procurement values above INR 500000. Apply the relevant procurement powers, publication and bidding-document requirements, allowing eligible unenlisted bidders. The manual describes a minimum 21-day opening timetable, subject to the stated considerations.
rules.application: Examine the proposed works tender route under Works Manual 3.5.1, its publication/bidding-document requirements and the applicable current delegation; the supplied edition describes open tendering above INR 500000.

rules.title: Works Manual 3.5.5 · Limited tender enquiry
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: The supplied edition describes limited tender enquiry below INR 500000 or the specified specialized/secret-work circumstances. Invite the selected enlisted contractors and publish as prescribed. Paragraph 3.5.5(ii)(b) specifies more than three invitees, with a recorded competent-authority exception where fewer approved bidders are available. Do not split demand to avoid open tendering or higher approval.
rules.application: For limited tendering, verify Works Manual 3.5.5's grounds, enlisted sources, prescribed invitations/publication and any recorded exception; do not import Assam RFQ thresholds into the central works route.

rules.title: Works Manual 3.5.7 · Single tender or nomination
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Single tender/nomination is restricted to the stated grounds, including qualifying urgency/emergency, proprietary expertise, security or justified continuation. The described continuation ground limits incremental work to 25% of the original contract value. Record and approve the reason and selected agency before single tendering, ensure market-consistent prices and avoid splitting.
rules.application: Under Works Manual 3.5.7, examine the specific permitted ground, prior approval and price reasonableness for a single-tender or nomination proposal; urgency alone is not an unrestricted procurement power.

rules.title: Works Manual 4.11 · Bid security and validity
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: The supplied edition generally describes bid security of 2–5% of estimated value, rounded to the nearest thousand rupees and specified in the bid documents, normally valid for 45 days beyond bid validity. It describes acceptable instruments, bid-securing declarations, permissible waivers and release/forfeiture conditions.
rules.application: Check the works bid-security requirement, permitted instrument/declaration or waiver, and the manual's 45-day additional validity under paragraph 4.11; keep this distinct from the Assam rule's 28-day provision.

rules.title: Works Manual 4.12–4.13 · Performance security and retention
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: The supplied edition describes performance security of 5–10% (usually 5% for works), and an exemption for contract value up to INR 100000. It normally specifies furnishing within 21 days of award and validity for 60 days beyond contractual obligations/DLP. Retention money is a separate contractual mechanism, usually 5% of running bills, with release conditions. Check current provisions and the actual contract.
rules.application: Distinguish performance security from running-bill retention under Works Manual 4.12–4.13, and examine the contract's amount, instrument, validity and release conditions against the applicable edition and amendments.

rules.title: Works Manual 5.1–5.3 · Evaluation and comparative note
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Evaluate against the disclosed tender criteria without introducing unverifiable conditions or relaxing material requirements. Follow the entity's Schedule of Procurement Powers for the accepting authority and committee. Paragraph 5.3 describes the signed comparative statement (with its LTE exception) and committee briefing note, including technical responsiveness, prices, taxes, discounts and ranking implications.
rules.application: Works Manual 5.1–5.3 calls for a transparent, criteria-based evaluation and the applicable signed comparative/briefing record under the entity's procurement powers; a quoted lowest price alone does not establish a responsive award.

rules.title: Works Manual 6.5.2 · Measurement and payment
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Record financially valued work in measurement/level books, with joint measurements. Interim payment certification checks actual quantities, field records, materials, extras, retentions/recoveries, approved variations and price adjustments. Final bills require completion and verification by the officer responsible for execution.
rules.application: For works payment, paragraph 6.5.2 requires reconciliation of the claimed quantities with measured work and the applicable certification, variations, deductions and recoveries before the bill is processed.

rules.title: Works Manual 6.6–6.7 · Handover and contract closure
rules.excerpt: Reviewed summary: Inspect/commission the completed work and obtain applicable occupancy/clearance records, as-built drawings, inventories and maintenance information. The completion report and final accounts record actual cost/time/components. Contract closure requires completed obligations/DLC and reconciliation of works, materials, user requirements and payments before final release of security.
rules.application: Works Manual 6.6–6.7 requires the handover documentation and completed-obligation, works/material and payment reconciliations to support contract closure and final security release.
